newsitem.title: UK: DHL says forwarders face modest future.
newsitem.headline: DHL says forwarders face modest future.

text.p: The future for freight forwarders "is rather modest compared to an exciting one foretold for express carriers", DHL International (UK) Ltd managing director, Nick Butcher said.

"International customers are looking for greater efficiency in their supply and distribution chains, thus freight forwarders are being squeezed out of a very competitive market by integrators, such as ourselves," he added in a statement.

Butcher was commenting on figures published in Boeing Co's latest World Air Cargo Forecast which estimate that the international express market will grow at an annual average rate of 18 percent over the next 20 years.
By 2015, Boeing forecast that the international air express market will account for 37 percent of the total international freight and mail market, compared to only five percent in 1995.
This compares with the air cargo industry's overall growth rate of 6.6 percent.

Butcher added that DHL "has significant market leadership and growth rates in excess of 20 percent a year..... we have investment plans in place, which will ensure that DHL maintains in its position."

Boeing also forecasts that by 2015, the express market will account for 29 percent of large freighters (over 50 tonnes capacity) against 22 percent in 1995, 62 percent of medium aircraft (30 to 50 tonnes) compared to 38 percent and 50 percent of small freighters (38 percent).
Key shareholders in DHL are Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Japan Airlines Co Ltd.
